audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly calls Nautilus's shield 'Riptide (W)'. Riptide is his E (three slowing explosions); the shield is Titan's Wrath (W, flat 12s). breakdown.early makes the mirror error — 'chase with R when his E shield is down'.
audit.why: The player is told to wait out the wrong ability. Riptide is a 7s-at-rank-1 slow he can throw every trade; Titan's Wrath is the 12s shield that actually decides whether the all-in is winnable.
audit.corrected: Shield named Titan's Wrath (W, 12s) with Riptide identified as the E slow, in spikes[0], early, mid and breakdown.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page claims 'your passive shrugs the first CC' and never mentions that Dredge Line grapples terrain.
audit.why: Mundo's passive resists only the FIRST Immobilizing effect. Staggering Blow roots on Nautilus's first attack against a target, so in practice that root spends the cannister and the hook, Riptide and Depth Charge all land at full effect. Separately, Dredge Line collides with terrain and pulls Nautilus to it, so he can cut off a retreat Mundo has no dash to answer — Flash is the only out.
audit.corrected: Both written in: phases[2].why now states the passive-vs-Staggering Blow order, spikes[0] adds the terrain grapple and the Flash rule.

audit.whatIsWrong: Dredge Line was listed at 15s in breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Depth Charge's cooldown appears nowhere.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14/13/12/11/10 and Depth Charge is 120/100/80. Those are the two numbers that define when Mundo can step up and when a gank converts.
audit.corrected: Real ranks written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and mid.

audit.why: Full phases and content win[] agree — Nautilus Levels 1-2, Skill at 3 and 4-5, Dr. Mundo from 6 on — and that reads correctly against a 53.06% winrate over 3992 games. The packet's own chart (Nautilus 4/7) is the outlier and is flagged as a defect in the packet itself; I did not propagate it. Only whys[3] contradicted its own Skill label and was rewritten.
audit.corrected: Chart left as-is; whys[3] corrected to match its Skill rating.

edits.before: Nautilus's Dredge Line (Q) plus a Riptide (W) shield lets him trade into you cleanly whenever your E is on cooldown, so respect his all-in windows and don't walk into wave-hidden hooks.
edits.after: Nautilus's Dredge Line (Q) plus a Titan's Wrath (W) shield lets him trade in whenever your E is down. It also grapples terrain to cut your retreat, and you have no dash — save Flash for that.

edits.before: Nautilus out-trades you at levels 1-2: his Q hook plus Staggering Blow passive stun and Riptide shield mean every all-in he starts lands more than yours, and your Q costs health you can't spare yet.
edits.after: Nautilus out-trades you at levels 1-2: Dredge Line plus Titan's Wrath's shield beat anything you start, and Staggering Blow's root eats your passive cannister on his first auto — so the hook lands in full.

edits.before: You stabilize at 3 once you have E Blunt Force Trauma to answer his burst, but a re-hook at 4-5 with Riptide up still favors him, and his level-6 Depth Charge lock keeps his gank threat higher than yours even after your R comes online.
edits.after: You stabilize at 3 with Blunt Force Trauma (E), but a re-hook at 4-5 with Titan's Wrath up still favors him — Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1, so step up inside that gap. Depth Charge (120s at rank 1) keeps his gank threat above yours.

edits.before: A level-4 re-hook with Riptide up tips the short trade back to Nautilus.
edits.after: At 4-5 a re-hook with Titan's Wrath up evens the short trade again.

edits.before: Naut hooks and chain-CCs but has no real kill threat. Dodge his Q, out-sustain him, and chase with R when his E shield is down. Track Dredge Line (Hook) before every step-up.
edits.after: Naut hooks and chain-CCs but has no real kill threat. His shield is Titan's Wrath (W, 12s); Riptide (E) only slows. Chase with R once the shield pops, and dodge the hook.

edits.before: Full kit online and your passive shrugs the first CC. Cleaver poke plus E-empowered swats start the grind; never brawl while Dredge Line (Hook) is up.
edits.after: Your passive eats only the FIRST immobilize — Staggering Blow's root usually spends it, so the hook still lands. Trade once Dredge Line is on cooldown.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook) (15s): matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Track it before every commit. - Your ultimate: spend it on kill windows, never on waves. - Summoners: track his Flash after any close call — it changes every dive call.
edits.after: - Dredge Line (14s at rank 1): his only engage — dodge it, then take the trade inside those 14 seconds. - Titan's Wrath (12s) is the shield; wait it out. - Depth Charge (120s at rank 1) is what turns a gank into a kill — track it, and his Flash.

edits.before: Track Nautilus’s Dredge Line (Hook) (15s): His only engage. Dodge it. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Track Dredge Line (14s at rank 1): his only engage, and it grapples terrain to cut your retreat too.

notes: The packet's suspectNames hit on 'Your Maximum Dosage' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Maximum Dosage is Dr. Mundo's own R and is spelled correctly.
